summary.text: The cosmic web is the network formed by galaxy filaments, the largest known structures in the universe.
Filaments are thread-like formations made of walls of galactic superclusters, commonly 50 to 80 megaparsecs long, and they form the boundaries between voids.
Because the universe's expansion is accelerating, the clusters making up filaments are moving apart faster, and in the far future they will dissolve.

facts.label: What they border
facts.value: Filaments form the boundaries between voids

facts.label: Discovery era
facts.value: Structures beyond superclusters found from the late 1980s

facts.label: Future
facts.value: In the far future they will dissolve

items.prompt: Mapping the universe, you find vast thread-like strings of galaxy clusters that mark the edges of voids. What do these threads together make up?

options.label: A single giant galaxy cluster
A ring around the Milky Way
The cosmic web, which shapes the observable universe
A set of unrelated, scattered clumps

items.explain: Galaxy filaments form the cosmic web and define the overall structure of the observable universe.

items.prompt: What will eventually happen to galaxy filaments, and why?

options.label: They will dissolve, as accelerating expansion pulls clusters apart
They will tighten into one giant galaxy as gravity wins
They will stay completely unchanged forever
They will dissolve, since their galaxies collide with each other

items.explain: Because of accelerating expansion, the clusters making up filaments move apart at an accelerated rate and in the far future will dissolve.

items.prompt: What are galaxy filaments built from?

options.label: Single stars strung out in very long lines
Great clouds of gas that hold no galaxies
Black holes lined up neatly end to end
Bound clusters of galaxies, joined into supercluster walls

items.explain: Filaments consist of walls of galactic superclusters, made of individual clusters of gravitationally bound galaxies.

items.prompt: Large quasar groups are among the largest structures known. How are they theorized to relate to filaments?

options.label: They are the empty voids between filaments
They may be early precursors of galaxy filaments
They are smaller pieces of single galaxies
They are filaments that have already dissolved

items.explain: Large quasar groups are theorized to be protohyperclusters or galaxy filament precursors.

items.prompt: A structure's cross-section is long and flat, much wider in one direction than the other. Which subtype of filament is it?

options.label: A galaxy wall
A filament subtype
A void
A supercluster

items.explain: The wall subtype has a significantly greater major axis than minor axis, while the filament subtype has roughly similar axes.

items.prompt: Typical filaments reach 50 to 80 megaparsecs, and the largest found, Quipu, reaches 400. About how many times longer than a typical filament is Quipu?

options.label: About the same length
Roughly twice as long
Roughly five to eight times
About a hundred times

items.explain: Quipu at 400 megaparsecs is about 5 to 8 times the common 50 to 80 megaparsecs.
